title: Spin-Independent Dissipation Induces Emergent Spin Mobility Polarization in Donor-Double-Stranded DNA-Acceptor Systems
authors: Hengrui Yang, Yu Xiong, Weitang Li, Zhigang Shuai
abstract: Despite extensive experiments, chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) remains debated. Using a donor-double-stranded DNA-acceptor model and Lindblad equation, we define spin mobility polarization via spin-resolved mean-square displacement and fix relaxation on a turnover plateau. Spin-independent relaxation locks the transient asymmetry from helical spin-orbit coupling (SOC) into a steady polarization. Weak SOC, expected to have little effect, boosts one spin but suppresses the other instead, in a "one enhanced, one suppressed" pattern. Flipping the helix exchanges them. The work defines mobility polarization as a probe and gives a generic dissipation-driven mechanism for CISS.
summary: The paper investigates the fundamental physics behind Chiral-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) using a DNA-based model simulated with the Lindblad master equation. It introduces 'mobility polarization' as a key diagnostic, demonstrating that spin-independent dissipation is necessary to stabilize the spin selectivity effect into a measurable steady state. This provides a general theoretical framework for understanding spin filtering in chiral molecular conductors.
main_problem: The microscopic origin of Chiral-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) remains highly debated, particularly regarding the necessity of spin-dependent versus spin-independent dissipation.
main_result: The study establishes that spin-independent dissipation is crucial for locking transient spin asymmetries into a steady polarization, revealing a generic 'one enhanced, one suppressed' mechanism universal to helical chiral structures.
method: The authors use the Lindblad master equation formalism applied to a donor-double-stranded DNA-acceptor model to calculate spin-resolved transport properties.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a Donor–double-stranded DNA–Acceptor (D–dsDNA–A) chain, governed by an extended Hamiltonian including helical Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC).
key_observables: Spin-resolved mean-square displacement ($	ext{MSD}$), mobility polarization ($P_v =  rac{D_\uparrow - D_\downarrow}{D_\uparrow + D_\downarrow}$), and the leading-time fraction ($f$).
important_parameters: Dissipation rates ($\Gamma, \Gamma_H$), helical SOC strength ($t_{SO}$), molecular length ($N$), and resonance energy windows ($\epsilon_D$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on modeling dissipation via Lindblad terms and distinguishing between dynamical mobility polarization ($p_v$) and steady-state spin accumulation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of $P_v$ on dissipation strength ($\Gamma$), showing optimal regimes, and demonstrate how the leading-time fraction ($f$) transitions from zero to unity as dissipation increases.
paper_structure: The paper develops a diagnostic tool ($P_v$) using MSD analysis within the Lindblad framework. It first shows that pure electronic models fail to yield steady polarization; subsequent inclusion of spin-independent dissipation locks this asymmetry, leading to the general 'one enhanced, one suppressed' pattern.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical mechanism for CISS based on open quantum system dynamics (dissipation), which is highly relevant to understanding charge transport in nanoscale molecular electronics and bio-hybrid devices.
